questions: Should the function assume the input DataFrame has exactly two columns named 'date' and 'closing_price', or should it handle other column names or additional columns gracefully?
Is the date column guaranteed to be in a format directly convertible by pd.to_datetime, or should the function handle parsing errors (e.g., different date string formats)?
Should the plot include any labels (title, x-axis, y-axis) or formatting, or is a bare scatter and line plot sufficient?
If the input DataFrame has fewer than two rows, should the function handle it (e.g., raise an error, return empty predictions) or assume at least two rows?
Should the predicted prices be rounded or formatted in any way (e.g., to two decimal places), or returned as raw floating-point numbers from model.predict?
Does 'next 7 days' mean 7 consecutive days starting from the day after the last date in the input, regardless of gaps in the input dates, or should it follow the input's time step?
Should the function close the matplotlib plot or leave it open for further modification by the caller?
Is the function required to handle timezone-aware dates, or can it assume naive timestamps?
